chunks: Whosoever is spared that Day will surely have mercy shown to him, and this will be a clear triumph.

key_terms.يَوْمَئِذٍ: that Day (referring to the Day of Judgment)

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to be spared on the Day of Judgment according to the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted as a promise of divine protection from the fires of Hell or major calamities, signifying that salvation is an act of pure mercy rather than mere merit. It underscores the concept of 'Fawz al-Mubin' (Clear Victory), where deliverance from divine wrath is the ultimate success for the believers. This aligns with the Shia emphasis on Allah's vast mercy preceding His wrath, offering hope to the faithful on the Day of Reckoning.
